title: Response Coherence & A/B Analysis — Sandbox Demo (Verdant Health)
next_steps: Samir to share sandbox access and pre-populated prompt set by 2027-01-14
Jules to run a short A/B benchmark with Verdant's sample dataset and share latency/cost spreadsheet by 2027-01-19
Verdant to confirm compliance contacts (security + legal) by 2027-01-18
action_items: Samir - setup Redwood sandbox workspace and invite Verdant team (due 2027-01-14)
Jules - run 500-sample A/B run (hosted vs quantized-dedicated) and upload results (due 2027-01-19)
Elena - share 2 canonical prompt sets and 1 regeneration policy doc (due 2027-01-17)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood's Eval/Quality tooling focusing on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Demoed console scenarios, API calls for batch evaluation, and outlined a pilot plan with benchmarks and security review.
topics: latency vs cost trade-offs (hosted vs dedicated)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Samir, AE with Redwood Inference. Appreciate you taking time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Elena: Hi this is Elena - head of ML at Verdant Health.
[00:11] Marcus: Marcus, infra/SRE.
[00:14] Priya: Priya, product.
[00:16] Tom: Tom, eng.
[00:18] Jules: Jules from Redwood, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll lead the demo.
[00:22] Samir: Great. Goal for today is a focused sandbox demo: show how Eval/quality monitoring handles prompt sets, regression alerts, and run an A/B compare scenario. We'll leave time for security questions at the end.
[00:34] Priya: Sounds good — our main instigators: coherence in patient triage responses and preventing hallucination on med guidance.
[00:42] Samir: Perfect. Elena, can you give 60s on current stack and success metrics?
[00:47] Elena: Sure — we use MajorCloudAI hosted endpoints for prod, but we've been seeing inconsistent phrasing and two types of failures: occasional hallucinated drug interactions and variations in tone that break UX. Our goals: reduce medically incorrect answers by 90% in triage workflow and keep 95th percentile latency under 350ms. We're exploring moving some inference to dedicated instances for sensitive traffic.
[01:12] Jules: Thanks. Quick clarifying — is data residency a hard requirement or preferred?
[01:16] Marcus: Preferred for now; full residency may be needed later. We do need SSO + audit logs.
[01:22] Samir: Good to know. Ok, demo time. I'll hand off to Jules.
[01:26] Jules: Cool. Jumping into the Redwood Console — first screen is the Eval workspace. On the left is Prompt Sets, then the Regression Rules tab, and A/B Experiments.
[01:36] [01:36] Jules: I'll open a pre-made prompt set called 'verdant-triage-v1' — it contains canonical prompts, expected annotations, and acceptance criteria. We often canonicalize prompts to reduce surface variance.
[01:47] Tom: Quick question — are these prompt sets versioned? We want to roll back easily.
[01:50] Jules: Yes, every prompt set has versions and diffs; you can pin a set to a route or a model version.
[01:56] [02:00] Jules: Now the neat bit: Regression Alerts. You can create rules on metrics like model accuracy (we support custom metrics), BLEU-ish similarity, or domain-specific flags — eg "med-hallucination-rate" which is based on an eval function you upload.
[02:16] Elena: How do you define 'med-hallucination-rate'? That sounds proprietary.
[02:20] Jules: It's user-defined — you provide a checker function or an eval harness. The console supports Python snippets or a webhook that returns pass/fail per sample. We run it across the prompt set and aggregate.
[02:32] [02:35] Speaker 3: Is there a latency hit from running these eval checks in real time?
[02:39] Jules: Usually we run them asynchronously as background jobs on sample sets. For live, lightweight checks (e.g., token-based filters), you can enable inline; heavier semantic checks are asynchronous to avoid production latency hit.
[02:49] Samir: I'll jump in — one common pattern is to run fast rule-based checks inline for immediate rejection, and run full evals nightly to trigger alerts.
[02:59] [03:05] Jules: Moving to A/B compare — here we set up an experiment splitting traffic 50/50. You can compare two model configurations or two prompt-set variants. The dashboard shows delta on custom metrics, latency, and cost per token.
[03:17] Priya: Are splits per-route? We have multiple endpoints for triage vs follow-up.
[03:21] Jules: Yes, splits are per-route and can be routed by policy (user cohort, geography). You can also pin VIP traffic to dedicated infra and let the rest be hosted.
[03:30] [03:36] Tom: Regarding infra, if we move to Dedicated, what's the upgrade path? Do we need code changes?
[03:40] Jules: Minimal — same API and SDK. Most customers just change endpoint config or routing policy in Console; we handle kernel selection and quantization profiles under the hood.
[03:49] Elena: Cost — curious about cost delta between hosted and dedicated when using quantized models.
[03:53] Samir: We'll share an itemized sheet, but rule of thumb: dedicated with int8 quantization can be 30-60% cheaper per-token depending on throughput. There's baseline infra commit costs for Dedicated.
[04:05] [04:12] Jules: Ok, live demo of A/B run — I'm going to upload a 500-sample prompt set (placeholder data) and kick an A/B job between hosted baseline (MajorCloudAI-like model) and Redwood-optimized quantized variant.
[04:22] [04:25] Jules: Job started. While that runs, open the 'Regressions' timeline — you can set alert windows and severity. E.g., critical if med-hallucination > 0.5% over 24h. You can route alerts to PagerDuty or send to Slack.
[04:40] Marcus: We need audit logs that show which prompt set triggered the alert and raw sample payload — is that available?
[04:46] Jules: Yes, each alert links to fingerprints of offending samples and you can export transcripts. Logs include prompt-set version, model version, and trace ids. For privacy, you can mask PII or use local evaluation in your VPC.
[04:58] [05:05] Priya: About masking — we do want to keep patient identifiers out of cloud copies. How does Redwood handle that?
[05:09] Jules: Two options: client-side anonymization before upload, or private eval runners in Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) where data never leaves your network. Both integrate with our Console.
[05:21] [05:27] Jules: A/B job finished. Results show delta: coherence score +7% for Redwood quantized, hallucination flag reduced from 1.8% to 0.6%; latency 95th went from 420ms -> 380ms; cost per 1k tokens reduced by ~42% in the quantized variant.
[05:44] Elena: Those numbers look promising — what's the statistical significance on 500 samples?
[05:48] Jules: It's indicative; we recommend at least 2-3k samples for production confidence. The console shows confidence intervals and p-values for the metrics.
[05:58] [06:05] Tom: The hallucination checker — can we plug our in-house clinical validator?
[06:09] Jules: Absolutely. You can reference an external validator via webhook or run a custom evaluation Docker image in our runner.
[06:16] Speaker 3: You mentioned KV cash earlier in docs — do you mean KV cache?
[06:20] Jules: Yeah, sorry for the typo — KV cache. Our runtime keeps a per-session KV cache that helps reduce cost for multi-turn dialogs.
[06:26] [06:32] Elena: For rollout, can we start with hosted for non-sensitive flows and gate clinical triage behind Private?
[06:36] Samir: That's a common architecture. Many customers run a split: non-PHI on hosted, PHI on Dedicated/Private. We can help define routing policies.
[06:44] [06:50] Marcus: Security specifics — SOC2 status? And do you support SAML SSO?
[06:54] Jules: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant (we provide a copy under NDA). We support SAML-based SSO, RBAC, KMS integrations; audit logs are retained per-configurable retention windows.
[07:05] Priya: Any peculiar gotchas when moving eval jobs into VPC?
[07:09] Jules: Mostly network egress configurations and endpoint whitelisting. We provide a deployment checklist and have automation for bootstrap.
[07:16] [07:25] Samir: Ok, switching to the API side quickly — Jules will demo the batch-eval API where you POST a prompt set and get back metrics and an artifact with per-sample flags.
[07:34] Jules: Here's a curl call: POST /v1/evals with JSON body pointing to S3 sample bucket; set model variants and metric hooks. The response includes job_id. Poll /jobs/{id} for results and then GET /jobs/{id}/artifacts to download CSV.
[07:50] Tom: Do those artifacts contain PII by default?
[07:52] Jules: They contain raw prompts unless you opt-in to masking. We can automatically redact based on regex or use your preprocessor.
[08:01] [08:10] Elena: One more thing — we need to be able to compare prompt variants (tone adjustment) and measure UX metrics (user satisfaction from in-app thumbs). Do you surface that?
[08:18] Jules: Yes, you can instrument a custom KPI (thumbs) and ingest signals back into Eval as a labeling job; the A/B dashboard will show that alongside model metrics.
[08:26] Priya: Nice.
[08:29] [08:35] Jules: Wrapping demo: artifacts I'll share after call — sandbox invite, pre-populated prompt sets, and the A/B job results CSV. Links: sandbox invite (link), redwood-eval-playbook.pdf (link), benchmark-template.csv (link).
[08:48] Marcus: For legal, we'll need data processing addendum and SOC2 report.
[08:52] Samir: We'll attach both in email after this call.
[08:56] Elena: Timeline — we'd like a pilot in the next 4 weeks, starting with 1 route. Is that feasible?
[09:03] Samir: Yes, feasible. Plan: 1) Sandbox and A/B runs (weeks 1–2), 2) pilot with 2k samples and security review (week 3), 3) production rollout after a successful sign-off (week 4).
[09:15] [09:20] Priya: Who's responsible on Redwood for the pilot?
[09:22] Samir: Jules will own technical execution; I'll be primary AE.
[09:26] Jules: I'll also set up a twice-weekly sync during pilot.
[09:30] [09:38] Tom: One more technical: can we get raw token-level traces for an example session?
[09:42] Jules: Yes, trace export includes token-level timings, kernel selections, and perf tags — can be anonymized.
[09:49] Elena: Great. That answers most of our concerns.
[09:52] Samir: Ok quick recap of next steps — send sandbox, run the expanded A/B benchmark, Elena to share canonical prompts and security contact. We'll have an MDT next Tuesday to review initial results.
[10:06] Priya: Accepted.
[10:07] Marcus: Thanks all.
[10:09] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the invite and docs. Meeting end.
